qa.question: Why might this comment have been outdated before the change?
qa.answer_markdown:
The old comment described the **previous implementation** of `ApproximateMemoryUsage()` — one that walked the arena's block list to sum allocated memory, which was genuinely O(blocks) and worth warning callers about.

Step S1 (referenced in the storyline overview) replaced that traversal with a **cached counter incremented at write time**. Once that landed, the function became O(1), but nobody updated the header comment on line 40. So the comment was outdated the moment S1 was merged — it described behavior the code no longer had.

This is a common drift pattern: implementation comments live in a different file from the implementation (`.h` vs `.cc`), so a change to the body in `memtable.cc` doesn't visually nudge the author to revisit the declaration in `memtable.h`. S3.1 is just the cleanup that should have ridden along with S1.

One nuance the new comment still glosses over (flagged in the **Behavior delta**): the cached counter tracks **entry bytes**, not **arena bytes**, so it's not just a faster version of the old number — it's measuring a slightly different thing.
